report.source_text: MRI of the thoracic and lumbar spine showed normal signal throughout the spinal cord parenchyma and was read as normal (figure 1). On retrospective review, subtle contrast enhancement of the leptomeninges surrounding the conus was noted (figure 2). MRI brain showed diffuse leptomeningitis. On retrospective review, linear radial perivascular enhancement surrounding the lateral ventricles was noted (figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 50s presented with one week of fever, nausea, vomiting, generalized weakness progressing to confusion, back pain, urinary hesitancy, lower extremity numbness and weakness. Neurologic exam revealed lower extremity weakness, ankle clonus, and upgoing toes. Initial MRI brain demonstrated diffuse leptomeningitis with linear radial perivascular enhancement; spinal MRI was normal with subtle leptomeningeal enhancement around the conus. CSF studies showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, normal glucose, and negative extensive infectious and neoplastic workup. Brain and meninges biopsy showed no infection. Autoimmune encephalitis antibody testing of CSF was positive for GFAP antibodies at high titer (1:128). Following immunotherapy including plasmapheresis, antimicrobials were stopped. Clinical improvement was documented with partial strength recovery before discharge and nearly full strength ambulatory status at 3-month follow-up. Repeat MRI demonstrated radiologic improvement consistent with treatment response.
